transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-07
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 min (recorded)
Attendees: Lena Torres (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Jared Kim (Redwood CSM), Oliver Kemp (Cranemere Head of Platform), Priya Shah (DevOps), Markus Vogel (CTO), Hannah Lee (PM)

Summary:
Quick renewal/expansion check-in focused on: committed capacity uplift, adding EU region (data sovereignty), burst/overage pricing, and pilot timeline for private VPC option. Customer brought new compliance timeline (Q4 audit) and wants clarity on SLA, audit logs and key management. Redwood to provide benchmark run and updated pricing amendment.

Topics:
- Committed capacity increase (baseline + burst)
- EU private VPC / data residency path
- Latency SLOs and canary strategy for multi-region traffic
- Security docs: SOC2, SSO, KMS integration
- Contract amendment process and procurement timeline

[00:00] Lena Torres: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, um just to set the agenda, quick renewal check-in, we have a couple items on committed capacity and then Marcus will talk through the performance benchmark plan. then we'll go into sovereignty and private vpc options. sound good?

[00:18] Oliver Kemp: yeah that works for us, thanks Lena. quick context: we are coming up on our contract renewal window in september and we need to lock in an uplift for the holiday season, and we also have a q4 data residency audit so the eu region is a hard requirement for some customers.

[00:34] Marcus Li: great, hi everyone. i'll keep the benchmark plan brief — objective is to validate token-level latency at your typical prompt mix and measure cost per 1k tokens under both hosted and private scenarios. we'll run 3 workloads: short chat queries (~32 tokens), mixed QA (~120 tokens), and long generation (~600 tokens) to simulate your support and transcript generation flows.

[00:57] Priya Shah: just to flag, our traffic is spiky — we do big batches at midnight in timezone eu-west and then a daytime chat peak in us-east. how does Redwood handle burst beyond committed pools? do we get throttled?

[01:12] Lena Torres: good question. so you have two levers: reserved capacity (committed) and burst capacity we can attach to the plan. if burst is used we bill at the burst rate — we can add a cap/overage policy so you don't go unlimited. also automatic fallback to a lower-cost compatible model is possible if latency SLOs are flexible.

[01:35] Markus Vogel: okay, what about routing? we can't have eu data leaving region, some of our compliance tests check that tokens are processed inside eu.

[01:44] Marcus Li: for that we recommend Redwood Private with a VPC control plane in eu-west. you can pin the model and route traffic locally. we maintain the same API surface so minimal app changes. there's an onprem option if you need air-gap, but that's heavier.

[02:05] Hannah Lee: timeline question — procurement asked whether we can have the private vpc provisioned before Oct 15, because audit is mid-Oct. is that realistic?

[02:14] Lena Torres: provision time depends on contract and infra sizing. for a standard private VPC we typically do a 4-6 week lead time once terms are signed and capacity is committed. given today's date, that puts provisioning mid-September if contract is signed by Aug 18. we should try to aim for that.

[02:36] Oliver Kemp: procurement will need a concrete contract amendment. can you send a commitment amendment with explicit start date, committed GPUs, and burst caps? and also the pricing tiers so our finance can model it.

[02:51] Lena Torres: yes — i'll send the amendment draft and updated pricing sheet today.

[03:00] Priya Shah: another technical point — we use an older transformer model internally; will Redwood's runtime support the kv cache and token streaming we rely on? i've had issues with other vendors dropping the stream after 2k tokens.

[03:16] Marcus Li: Redwood's runtime supports continuous KV cache and streaming; there are a couple knobs — max prefix, session pooling — we'll surface the default config and also run your benchmark to exercise long sessions so you can see any degradation. some transcriptions might have slight errors in names but core behavior should be solid.

[03:42] Markus Vogel: in terms of cost, how does dedicated compare to hosted? we are trying to decide if purchasing a dedicated pool with reserved capacity makes sense versus staying hosted and paying higher per-token price with burst.

[03:54] Lena Torres: typically for sustained throughput — if you have predictable monthly token volumes — dedicated/reserved is 30-55% cheaper vs pure hosted; exact depends on model family and quantization. Redwood Optimize will provide suggestions like lighter quantization for batch jobs and batching config to lower per-token cost. we'll include cost modeling in the spreadsheet.

[04:18] Hannah Lee: can you also include examples of automatic fallbacks? we need documented behaviour if eu capacity is saturated during peak.

[04:26] Marcus Li: yes — fallback policies are configurable: region-fallback (route to another eu cluster), model-fallback (drop to smaller quantized variant), or rate-limiting with 503 and retry headers. we'll show config snippets in the playbook.

[04:44] Priya Shah: security — we need SSO (SAML), RBAC, audit logs shipped to our splunk. do you support customer-managed KMS with HSM?

[04:56] Lena Torres: short answer yes: SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning, RBAC at token/route level, and audit logs can be streamed to your SIEM. for encryption we support customer-managed KMS for private deployments — HSM is an enterprise add-on. i'll attach the security pack link after the call: https://redwood.ai/security-pack (note: link for reference).

[05:20] Oliver Kemp: can we get a copy of SOC2 and penetration test reports?

[05:26] Jared Kim: absolutely — i'll drop SOC2 Type II summary and the latest pen test redacted artifacts, plus architecture diagrams.

[05:35] Markus Vogel: about benchmarks — Marcus, what metrics will you return? p50/p95/p99 latencies, token throughput, and cost-per-1k?

[05:44] Marcus Li: yes p50/p95/p99, tail latencies on long prompts, throughput in tokens/sec, and cost per 1k tokens under both hosted and private configs. we'll also provide a CSV with request-by-request timings so you can plug into your dashboards.

[06:02] Priya Shah: got it. also, please include a test that simulates our midnight batch job, because that one hits 4x the daytime load.

[06:09] Marcus Li: yep we'll add a spiky workload. question for you: do you have any hard latency SLOs for interactive chat?

[06:17] Oliver Kemp: under 250ms p95 for the short chat path; for long gen we are ok up to 2s p95 but we want predictable tails.

[06:26] Lena Torres: we can tune pooling, batching, and model choice to hit 250ms p95 on short queries; we'll validate in the benchmark. if not we can propose a dedicated reserved slice sized for your peak.

[06:40] Hannah Lee: procurement will probably ask about termination clauses and credit for downtime. what's Redwood's SLA?

[06:47] Lena Torres: hosted offers 99.9% uptime SLA, dedicated private plans have higher SLAs available as enterprise add-on. credits depend on incident severity and are spelled out in the TOS. we'll include SLA section in the amendment draft.

[07:05] Markus Vogel: any chance to pilot EU private cluster before commit? we'd prefer a short validation run with sample traffic before signing a long-term reserved contract.

[07:14] Jared Kim: yes, we can do a 14-day pilot with limited capacity, or a paid PoC that converts to committed capacity. Marcus can stand up a sandbox in eu-west for you.

[07:26] Marcus Li: process: we provision sandbox with limited nodes, run the benchmark, and then iterate. it'll surface any network egress or config changes you need.

[07:36] Priya Shah: do you support customer-side NAT for egress? our infra team needs to control egress IPs for allowlists.

[07:43] Marcus Li: yes for private VPC we can use customer-controlled NAT and IP whitelisting. we'll document the network diagram and firewall rules.

[07:57] Oliver Kemp: a concern — Anthropic offered us a short-term discount to lock in now; how flexible is Redwood on term length and ramped billing? we might want a 6-month ramp to avoid committing full capacity immediately.

[08:12] Lena Torres: we can do stepped commitments (ramped capacity) with a defined ramp schedule in the amendment. pricing will reflect the ramp. if you need a short-term discount we can also propose a limited pilot discount to bridge procurement.

[08:28] Hannah Lee: thanks — that's helpful. one more — can we schedule a deep-dive with networking team to discuss VPC peering and routing specifics?

[08:35] Lena Torres: yes — Marcus and Jared can meet your network folks. i'll let Jared coordinate calendar invites.

[08:44] [Slight crosstalk / someone types in chat]

[08:50] Marcus Li: we'll run the benchmark next Tuesday (Aug 12) unless you prefer a different date. we need a small sample dataset and a list of endpoints to emulate.

[08:59] Priya Shah: Aug 12 works. i'll upload a sanitized sample dataset and a short prompt set by Aug 11.

[09:07] Lena Torres: perfect. recap quick: 1) Redwood to send amendment + pricing (Lena) 2) SE to run benchmarks and share CSV + results (Marcus) 3) CSM to share security docs and SOC2 (Jared) 4) Cranemere to confirm procurement timeline and upload sample dataset (Oliver/Priya). we will reconvene Sept 2 to review amendment.

[09:31] Oliver Kemp: that aligns. any blockers on your side?

[09:36] Lena Torres: none. we'll aim to get materials out today and have the benchmark results by Aug 13.

[09:45] Markus Vogel: thanks everyone — looking forward to results.

[09:51] Jared Kim: i'll create the sandbox project and send invites; expect the security pack link and SOC2 within the hour.

[10:00] [Meeting ends]

Notes on transcription quality: occasional word swaps (e g 'kv' transcribed as 'k v'), some speaker label slippage in a few short segments; overall medium quality.
